notes.1a: This was generally correct, although if a wrong answer was given, the method mark was sometimes awarded for showing 110x5+85x3.
notes.1ci: This was well answered although some candidates did not recognise the significance of the ratio of adults to children of 3:2 requiring a division of 5 to obtain the final answer.
notes.1cii: The majority of candidates answered this part well, although many found this part challenging. Some candidates did not calculate the two total costs so could not complete the required ratio.
notes.1d: This was generally well answered. A few candidates only calculated the increase in the cost of the ticket rather than the new cost.
notes.1e: Some candidates appeared to have difficulty with this part as it dealt with a percentage decrease. The common error seen was to divide by 2.7 rather than 3.
notes.2a: Many accurate triangles were drawn. Some candidates did not include the arcs or misread the question and inverted the lengths of QR and PR.
notes.2bi: Candidates generally understood how to find a perpendicular bisector. The common errors were to omit the construction arcs or to be inaccurate in their drawing.
notes.2bii: Candidates generally understood how to find an angle bisector. The common errors were to omit the construction arcs or to be inaccurate in their drawing. A fair proportion of candidates did not attempt this part.
notes.2c: Some candidates did show that they understood how to find the necessary region. However this was the least successful part of the question.
notes.2d: Although some candidates measured the length QR and used the correct scaling many could not make the necessary conversion from centimetres to kilometres.
notes.3a: Nearly all candidates gave the correct answer.
notes.3b: Many candidates recognised that the required answer was obtained from finding a quarter of the total number.
notes.3c: A small majority of candidates gave the correct answer. Some candidates did not recognise that the modal number will come from the largest sector of the pie chart.
notes.3di: Generally candidates could fill in the frequency table.
notes.3dii: Many candidates understood how to calculate the mean from a frequency table. Only a few candidates obtained the correct answer for this part. However some candidates gained marks for showing their working. A common error was to evaluate 40x0 as 40 instead of 0.
notes.3ei: Candidates understood how to obtain this probability. There are fewer instances of candidates giving answers as ratios, the overwhelming majority of candidates giving the answer as a fraction (although not necessarily in its lowest form), a percentage or a decimal.
notes.3eii: Some candidates correctly evaluated this probability. The common error was to evaluate the probability of obtaining only one point as opposed to at least one point.
notes.3eiii: Candidates were much better this year in understanding that if an event is impossible then the probability must be zero.
notes.3f: A majority of candidates obtained the correct answer. The common error was to give a wrong answer with no working. 100 310

notes.5ai: The table was generally correctly completed.
